title: Short-term hypoxia mobilizes iron-bound phosphorus in a drinking-water reservoir: a laboratory core incubation
abstract: Hypolimnetic hypoxia is a growing concern in stratified drinking-water reservoirs, yet the short-term response of sediment phosphorus release to oxygen depletion remains poorly constrained. This fictional demonstration study incubated intact sediment cores from three sites under normoxia, hypoxia, and hypoxia with nitrate addition for 21 days. Hypoxia increased overlying SRP from 0.02 to 0.84 mg/L, Fe-bound P declined by 31%, and the estimated diffusive flux was 7.8 times higher than under normoxia. Nitrate reduced the hypoxic increase by 58% but did not prevent Fe-bound P loss.
summary: 21 天缺氧培养使水库沉积物 Fe–P 快速释放，上覆水 SRP 由 0.02 升至 0.84 mg/L；硝酸盐可削减 58% 的释放但不能阻止 Fe–P 损失。
